region.name: Snowflake Cost And Migration
region.summary: Covers the decisions and incidents involving the team's data infrastructure: the February 2026 Snowflake cost-spike response and the move of real-time ML features from Snowflake to Postgres instead of buying a feature store, plus related platform migrations like push notifications and the backend tech stack.

brief.text:
**What this region covers**
Two linked data-infrastructure efforts from 2026: the February Snowflake cost spike and its remediation, and ADR-030 (Accepted), moving real-time ML feature computation from Snowflake to Postgres. It also touches a push-notification migration to Customer.io and the Senior Backend Engineer stack.

**Recent changes**
- Devon Park completed five fixes: dashboard refresh moved from 5 minutes to hourly (about $115/day to $9/day), an aggregation-table query hint (about $2/day), per-warehouse monitoring with a daily Slack digest, a required estimated-daily-cost field on new dashboards, and a monthly spend review.
- Maya concluded the spike was internal usage, not vendor behavior.

**Decisions**
- ADR-030: compute about 30 personalization features per user (about 3.6M rows) in Postgres on application writes, served in under 100ms. It replaces a brittle nightly export with 24-hour latency.
- Rejected a feature store (Tecton $200k+/yr; Feast adds operational burden). Postgres costs about $0 incremental.
- Snowflake stays for raw events, dashboards, offline training and analytics.
- Non-goals: buying a feature store, moving analytics off Snowflake, running longer than three months.
- Add per-warehouse spend monitoring with a Slack digest of the top 5 costliest queries.
- Buy Customer.io rather than extend direct FCM/APNs.

**Open questions**
- Feature drift, write load and model degradation risks, owned by Kavi Raman. Mitigation: a nightly comparison job and at least four weeks of parallel running.
- Customer.io risks: delivery-rate drop during cutover, about $4–6k/month at 100k campaigns, and vendor lock-in.
- Data/ML has no dedicated team; it is a two-person side job.

**Suggested next steps**
- Confirm the status of the phased migration (planned May–August; phases June–August). Today is October, so check whether it finished.
- Verify Phase 1 (top 10 features on the parallel Postgres path) and the parallel-run comparison results.
- Keep the monthly cloud spend review going with Maya, Devon and Marcus Bell.

items.title: Decision: Add per-warehouse spend monitoring and Slack digest
items.summary: Medium-term fix: per-warehouse spend monitoring in Snowflake plus a daily Slack digest of the top 5 most expensive queries.

items.title: Decision: Buy delivery reliability and growth tooling rather than extend direct FCM/APNs
items.summary: Problems are not solved by more code on the same architecture, so use third-party providers.
